# CreateListener <img class="product" src="media/b3d-20x14.png" alt="Blitz3D" title="Blitz3D" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [3D Sound](Blitz3D-3D-Sound)

</div>


```blitzbasic
CreateListener:Int32 parent:Int32, rolloff_factor:Float32=1, doppler_scale:Float32=1, distance_scale:Float32=1
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `parent` | In | Int32 | required | The entity that carries the listener, typically the camera. |
| `rolloff_factor` | In | Float32 | `1` | How fast sounds get quiet with distance: 0 means they do not, 1 is the normal rate and above that makes them fade faster. Defaults to 1. |
| `doppler_scale` | In | Float32 | `1` | How strong the pitch change of moving sounds is: 0 turns it off, 1 is the real one and 2 shifts twice as far. Defaults to 1. |
| `distance_scale` | In | Float32 | `1` | How many meters one unit of your world is, which sets the distances that volume falls off over and how fast things move for the doppler shift. Defaults to 1. |

**Returns:** The entity handle of the listener, as in the original. It sits at the position of the parent and can be moved, turned, parented and freed like any other entity; EntityClass says "Listener".

## Description

Creates the ear that 3D sounds are heard with. It is carried by another entity, usually the camera, so that sounds get quieter with distance and move between the left and right speaker as the listener moves and turns. Only one listener is used at a time. The listener has to exist before [EmitSound](EmitSound) is used.

The three options can be changed afterwards, and glide to their new values, with [ListenerRolloff](ListenerRolloff), [ListenerDoppler](ListenerDoppler) and [ListenerDistance](ListenerDistance); [SpeedOfSound](SpeedOfSound), [ListenerRadius](ListenerRadius) and [ListenerFalloff](ListenerFalloff) change the rest. To move the ear to another entity, free the listener with FreeEntity and call CreateListener again, as in the original.

## Differences

* Volume falls off as 1 / (1 + rolloff * meters * 0.05), which is gentler than the curve of the original: the original (FMOD 3) is at full volume up to one meter and then falls off as meters ^ -rolloff, so at 20 meters with rolloff 1 it is at 5% where this runtime is at 50%. [SetFalloff](SetFalloff) picks the curve for the sounds that start after it and [SetChannelFalloff](SetChannelFalloff) for one channel (`0` is `new`, `1` is `legacy`, `2` is `soloud`). Without a call the environment variable `BLITZLLVM_VOLUME_FALLOFF` picks it: `new` (or unset) is the one above, `legacy` is the one of the original (checked by ear against Blitz3D 1.118; the original is noisier, since it opened FMOD at 44.1 kHz and 16 bits as common sound devices of Windows 98 wanted), and `soloud` is the one of SoLoud (the audio library of the SoLoud builds of Blitz3D), 1 / (1 + rolloff * (meters - 1)) from a meter on, which is the same as `legacy` for a rolloff of 1.
* The pitch follows the speeds along the line between the listener and the sound, with sound moving at 340 meters per second (or what [SpeedOfSound](SpeedOfSound) sets). Speeds are measured from how far the entities moved in their last step, so a sound that comes from an entity that was placed somewhere (and not moved) has no shift; nothing moves faster than 90% of the speed of sound as far as the shift is concerned. The shift follows a change of the speeds over about 10 milliseconds (at any frame rate), so a change of speed is heard right away and the pitch still glides from one value to the next, not stepping at every frame.
* Samples of a source that drives past the listener at 60 meters per second, recorded with tools/render_doppler_samples.py: [doppler_off.ogg](media/audio/doppler_off.ogg) (doppler scale 0, steady 441 Hz), [doppler_on.ogg](media/audio/doppler_on.ogg) (scale 1, about 535 Hz while it comes closer, dropping to 375 Hz within a few frames of passing and staying there while it leaves) and [doppler_far.ogg](media/audio/doppler_far.ogg) (distance scale 0.25, so the speeds are a quarter and the shift is smaller).
* Samples of a source that moves away from 1 to 61 meters in two seconds (doppler off, rolloff 1), recorded with tools/render_falloff_samples.py: [falloff_new.ogg](media/audio/falloff_new.ogg) (fades to about 30%), [falloff_soloud.ogg](media/audio/falloff_soloud.ogg) and [falloff_legacy.ogg](media/audio/falloff_legacy.ogg) (both fade to under 2%).

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
camera = CreateCamera()
listener = CreateListener(camera)

source = CreateSphere()
PositionEntity source, 10, 0, 20
sound = Load3DSound("engine.wav")
LoopSound sound
EmitSound sound, source

While Not KeyHit(1)
	TurnEntity camera, 0, 0.5, 0
	RenderWorld
	Flip
Wend
```
